## INITIAL EPISODE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)
Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic
therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,
etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved
or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the
diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to
antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial
therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.
## Inpatient

## Patient at increased risk of CDI recurrence:
(e.g., age >65 years old, concomitant antibiotic use during CDI treatment,
and/or immunosuppression)
Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days [M]
## Patient not meeting criteria above for increased risk of CDI recurrence:
Vancomycin 125mg PO q6h for 10 days [M]

## Outpatient

## Treatment for initial episode of CDI:
Non-VA order for above
## Alternate treatment for patient at increased risk of CDI recurrence:
(e.g., age >65 years old, concomitant antibiotic use during CDI treatment,
and/or immunosuppression)
